subject: math-aa-sl
about: Original practice questions written for NevaIB from the IB guide's syllabus understandings and the school's unit order. Not IB past-paper questions, not publisher material and not IB markschemes: the marking points are written for self-marking. Organisms, experiments and data in data-response items are invented for practice.

items.note: Multiply by π/180: 135 × π/180 = 3π/4. Learn 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° multiples as fractions of π.

items.stem: A sector has radius 5 cm and angle 1.2 radians. What is its arc length?
items.note: Arc length l = rθ = 5 × 1.2 = 6 cm (θ in radians). 15 cm² is the sector area ½r²θ.

items.stem: What is the exact value of cos(π/3)?
items.note: cos 60° = 1/2, sin 60° = √3/2. Use the 30-60-90 triangle with sides 1, √3, 2.

items.stem: Find the distance between the points (1, 2, −3) and (4, −2, 9).
items.note: d = √(3² + (−4)² + 12²) = √169 = 13. 169 is d² — remember the square root.

items.stem: In triangle ABC, a = 8 cm, A = 40° and B = 65°. Find b to 3 significant figures.
items.note: Sine rule: b = a sin B ÷ sin A = 8 sin 65° ÷ sin 40° = 11.3 cm. Check the calculator is in degrees.

items.stem: A triangle has sides 5, 7 and 8. Find the angle opposite the side of length 7.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 6 cm and 10 cm and included angle 30°.
items.note: Area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 6 × 10 × sin 30° = 15 cm². The angle must be between the two sides used.

items.stem: Given that sin x = 3/5 and x is obtuse, find cos x.
items.note: cos²x = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25, so cos x = ±4/5. Obtuse (second quadrant) → cosine negative.

items.stem: Using the same x (sin x = 3/5, x obtuse), find sin 2x.
From a point 85.8 m from the base of a vertical tower on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top is 25°. Find the height of the tower.
items.note: tan 25° = h ÷ 85.8, so h = 85.8 tan 25° = 40.0 m. 36.3 = 85.8 sin 25° (uses the wrong ratio).

items.stem: A cuboid measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm (height). Find the angle between the space diagonal and the base.
items.note: Base diagonal = √(3² + 4²) = 5. tan θ = 12/5 → θ = 67.4°. The angle with a plane uses the projection of the line onto that plane.

items.stem: In triangle ABC, a = 6, b = 8 and A = 40°. Which statement is true?
choices: There is exactly one triangle, with B ≈ 59.0°
No triangle exists because b > a
There is exactly one triangle, with B ≈ 121.0°
There are two possible triangles, with B ≈ 59.0° or B ≈ 121.0°
items.note: sin B = 8 sin 40° ÷ 6 = 0.857. Both B and 180° − B work, since 121.0° + 40° < 180°. That is the ambiguous case.

items.stem: A sector OAB has radius 10 cm and angle AOB = 0.8 radians. (a) Find the perimeter of the sector. (b) Find the area of the segment between chord AB and arc AB.
markscheme: (b) Sector area = ½ × 100 × 0.8 = 40 cm²; triangle = ½ × 100 × sin 0.8 = 35.87 cm² (1)
items.tactic: Segment = sector − triangle. The calculator must be in radians for sin 0.8.

markscheme: x = 5π/6 (second solution from the symmetry of the unit circle) (1)
items.tactic: List every solution in the domain: draw the unit circle or the graph to find the second one.

items.stem: Show that (sin x + cos x)² = 1 + sin 2x, and hence find the exact value of (sin(π/12) + cos(π/12))².
markscheme: Expand: sin²x + 2 sin x cos x + cos²x (1)
Use sin²x + cos²x = 1 and 2 sin x cos x = sin 2x to get 1 + sin 2x (1)
With x = π/12, 2x = π/6 and sin(π/6) = 1/2 (1)
items.tactic: "Show that": every line must follow from the one before; finish with the target expression.

items.stem: A ship sails 12 km on a bearing of 050° from port P to point Q, then 9 km on a bearing of 150° to point R. (a) Show that angle PQR = 80°. (b) Find PR. (c) Find the bearing of R from P.
markscheme: (a) Back bearing of P from Q = 230°; angle PQR = 230° − 150° = 80° (1)
(c) sin QPR = 9 sin 80° ÷ 13.69, so angle QPR = 40.3° (1)
items.tactic: Bearings: draw north lines at every point and mark the back bearing before using the cosine rule.
